metadata.note: The Syracuse and Binghamton Railroad and its successor the Lackawanna Syracuse Branch -- the north-south line up the Tioughnioga valley through Whitney Point, Marathon and Cortland. Chartered Aug 18 1851 to bring Pennsylvania coal to fuel Syracuse's salt industry, consolidated with the Oswego and Syracuse in 1853, and opened over its full 81 miles from Geddes to Binghamton on Oct 18 1854. It foreclosed almost at once: the line was sold in 1856 to the Syracuse and Southern Railroad, renamed the Syracuse, Binghamton and New York Railroad on Apr 30 1857. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western bought it in 1869 and leased the Oswego and Syracuse on Feb 13 1869, assembling a 114-mile, thirty-station branch from Binghamton through Syracuse to Oswego on Lake Ontario -- a north-south artery for its anthracite. Passenger service between Syracuse and Binghamton ended in September 1958, and on the Syracuse-Oswego half on Feb 13 1949. This layer covers the Binghamton-Syracuse half; oswego_syracuse.geojson covers the rest of the same branch.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Every headway and speed is an estimate; no timetable has been consulted for any era. September 1958 is the month passenger service ended, not a dated last train. The 1856 sale and the Apr 30 1857 renaming are documented but the Syracuse and Southern Railroad name lasted under a year and is folded into the second feature's note rather than being drawn as its own era. Intermediate opening dates do not exist in the sources -- the line is documented as opening over its full length at once on Oct 18 1854, so no progressive build-out is shown. The station list is not sourced beyond the towns the trace passes and the handful nyrails names; thirty stations are documented for the whole Binghamton-Oswego branch but not enumerated. The drawn line follows the surviving and abandoned alignment as mapped today, which for a line lifted after 1958 may differ in places from the 1854 route.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

It had been consolidated with the Oswego and Syracuse Railroad in 1853 under an act of the state legislature, giving a through line from Binghamton to Lake Ontario. Frequency estimated/unsourced

properties.geometry_source: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (ODbL): railway ways -- active, abandoned, disused and dismantled -- plus named rail trails were fetched from Overpass for the corridor, filtered to those within 1.6 km of the Commons route (Data:Syracuse and Binghamton Railroad.map, CC BY 4.0), and a shortest path run from the Binghamton end to Geddes. 1367 points, 81.95 mi. The Commons trace was used as the corridor guide only, not as the drawn geometry: it carries a 7.1 km and a 5.8 km straight jump either side of index 274, which the OSM trace fills with real alignment.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, 1367 points, median vertex spacing 58 m and 90th percentile 200 m; 5 of the 1366 steps exceed 1 km, the longest 1.7 km, on stretches where the line is lifted and only sparse abandoned-railway geometry survives. No leg is a drawn straight-line approximation. Traced 81.95 mi against the 81 miles the company gave for Geddes to Binghamton and 81.97 mi for the independent Commons digitization of the same corridor.

segments.note: The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western bought the Syracuse, Binghamton and New York in 1869 and leased the Oswego and Syracuse on Feb 13 1869, giving it a branch from Binghamton north through Syracuse to the Lake Ontario port at Oswego -- about 114 miles and thirty stations in all, built to move its anthracite. This feature is the Binghamton-Syracuse half; see oswego_syracuse.geojson for Syracuse-Oswego. Frequency estimated/unsourced

segments.note: The branch met the DL&W main line at Binghamton, the Utica Branch at Chenango Forks (see utica_chenango_susquehanna_valley_railway.geojson -- UC&SV trains used these tracks between Chenango Forks and Binghamton) and the Cincinnatus Branch at Cortland Junction. Passenger service between Syracuse and Binghamton ended in September 1958. Freight continued, to Conrail in 1976 and the New York, Susquehanna and Western from 1982 to 1995; much of the right of way south of Cortland is now lifted. Frequency estimated/unsourced
